title: The son on the mountain
hook: Nuh's own son refuses the ark, says a mountain will save him, and the waves come between them (11:42–43)

segments.voice: Yesterday: building on dry land, Nuh with his hammer while the town laughed. Your line was build before the rain. What odd right thing did you do? Day thirty-one.
screen: `BUILDING ON DRY LAND — BUILD BEFORE THE RAIN.`

segments.voice: Almost every family has someone like this. The one you can't reach. The brother who stopped answering. The daughter who moved across the country and calls twice a year. The father who'd rather argue than listen. You love them. You've tried everything. And they're still out there, on the other side of something you can't cross. Today is the last day of Nuh's story. The rain has come, the ship is afloat, and the story, which has been about a whole people, suddenly narrows to a single face. Nuh's own son, standing apart, as the water rises.
screen: `THE ONE YOU CAN'T REACH.` → `THE SHIP IS AFLOAT.` → `ONE FACE, AS THE WATER RISES.`

segments.voice: Surah eleven. The ship sails, the Qur'an says, through waves like mountains. And Nuh sees his son, standing apart. And he calls to him, in Pickthall's words: “O my son! Come ride with us.” Listen to that. After nine hundred and fifty years of calling strangers, the last call in the story is a father calling his child. And the son answers, paraphrasing: I'll go up a mountain; it will keep me safe from the water. He trusts the highest thing he can see. Nuh answers: today nothing can protect from God's command, except for the one He has mercy on. And then one of the saddest lines in the Qur'an: “And the wave came in between them.” That's all. No speech. A wave, between a father and a son. The Qur'an doesn't name the son; tradition calls him Kan'an. But it doesn't end there. When the water settles and the ship rests on a mountain called al-Judi, Nuh turns to God. Paraphrasing: my Lord, my son was of my family, and Your promise is true. He's still calling, even now. And God answers him gently but firmly: he is not of your family, his conduct was not right; don't ask Me about what you don't know. And Nuh, the great prophet, asks forgiveness for even asking. Commentators have written a great deal about this. Many say family, in this answer, means the family of faith, not blood. What everyone notices is the father. A prophet who could accept anything from God, still reaching for his son, right to the end.
screen: `WAVES LIKE MOUNTAINS.` · `O MY SON! COME RIDE WITH US.` · `I'LL GO UP A MOUNTAIN.` · `STILL ASKING, AFTER THE FLOOD.` · then, large: `THE WAVE CAME IN BETWEEN THEM.`

segments.voice: The bell will give you two minutes. Bring to mind someone you can't reach right now. Someone far away, or estranged, or just closed off. See their face. Don't rehearse the argument. Don't plan what you'll say. Just hold them. If you pray, pray for them, in your own words, the way Nuh kept asking for his son. If you don't, wish them well, silently, as if across water. The bell holds the time.
The son on the mountain. Nuh's son, who trusted a mountain over the ship, and the father who called him to the last.
screen: `THE SON ON THE MOUNTAIN — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: a father still calls. Today, send one small message to someone you can't reach. No argument, no pressure. Just: thinking of you. Day thirty-one.

howItsDone: Muslims read Nuh's call to his son in surah eleven, and many parents recall it when a child has turned away: faith can't be handed down, but a parent keeps praying.

fork.setup: you're Nuh. the ship is moving through waves like mountains, and you see your son standing apart. what do you do?
options: say nothing; he made his choice.
call to him: come ride with us.
turn the ship toward him by force.
fork.reveal: "O my son! Come ride with us." he said a mountain would save him. and the wave came in between them.

original.note: Arabic: "O my little son," a tender form Nuh uses in 11:42; Luqman uses it too.

trapdoor: what you thought: everyone in Noah's family got on the ark.
what it means: the son on the mountain — Nuh's own son refused the ship, trusting a mountain, and the wave came between them.
what a scholar hears: ya bunayya, a tender diminutive; 11:45–46, where God says he is not of your family, is read by many as the family of faith; and the ship rests on al-Judi (11:44).

sources.quoted: O my son! Come ride with us
And the wave came in between them

sources.ref: Qur'an 11:43–47 (the mountain; al-Judi; Nuh's plea and God's answer)

notes: Pickthall 11:42–43 quoted from memory ('...and Noah cried unto his son - and he was standing aloof - O my son! Come ride with us, and be not with the disbelievers.' / '...And the wave came in between them, so he was among the drowned.'). Confirm.
The son's name Kan'an (or Yam) comes from tradition. Confirm.
11:46 ('he is not of thy household; lo! he is of evil conduct'): paraphrased as 'his conduct was not right'. Commentators' reading as the family of faith is the majority; confirm phrasing.
Original: ya bunayya (diminutive of ibn). Luqman uses it in 31:13; confirm the note.
Practice invites praying for someone 'in your own words' or wishing them well; no prayer text written.
